approach: In a rigid insulated cylinder the gas does no external work, so the heat supplied equals the rise in internal energy from the change in degrees of freedom.

steps.text: Write the initial internal energy of the 4 moles of diatomic gas.
After dissociation, 2 moles of diatomic gas remain, and the other 2 moles turn into 4 moles of monatomic gas.
Write the final internal energy at the same temperature T.
steps.why_this_step: Each remaining diatomic molecule still has 5 degrees of freedom, and each new atom has only 3 translational degrees of freedom.

steps.text: Since the cylinder is rigid, no work is done, so the heat supplied equals the change in internal energy.

common_mistakes.text: Misreading the question as if all 4 moles dissociate, instead of only 2, gives a final internal energy of 12RT and a change of 2RT.
